notes.precedence: If a path matches both framework_paths and personal_paths, personal_paths WINS. The personal list is a guard — update.js must check personal_paths FIRST and skip any file that matches, even if framework_paths would otherwise select it.
notes.example_files_are_framework: Any file matching **/*.example is always FRAMEWORK-owned, regardless of what directory it lives in. This includes .secops/foundry.yaml.example, .env.example, and any future *.example files under .secops/ or .squad/. update.js must sync these even when they sit alongside personal YAML files.
notes.secops_live_yaml_is_personal: All .secops/**/*.yaml files that are NOT *.example are personal. They contain consumer-specific workspace IDs, tenant IDs, environment topology, and configuration specific to the consumer's org. update.js must never overwrite or delete them.
notes.secops_readme_and_docs_are_framework: README.md files within .secops/ subtree (e.g. .secops/README.md, .secops/alerting/README.md, .secops/identity/README.md) are framework documentation and ARE included in framework_paths via '.secops/**/README.md' — however those files are NOT currently in framework_paths above because the .secops/ tree as a whole is personal domain. update.js should NOT sync .secops/ subtree contents AT ALL except *.example files (handled by the **/*.example rule). The .secops/ README files may be updated by consumers freely.
notes.agent_charters_are_personal: '.squad/agents/{name}/charter.md' is the consumer's SPECIFIC cast for that agent — their voice, their codebase context, their rules. It MUST NOT be overwritten on update. The TEMPLATE for a new charter lives at '.squad/templates/charter.md' and is framework-owned (synced on update). Charters are only generated at install time from the template; they are never re-generated by update. Consumers own their charter content.
notes.consumer_skills_are_personal: '.squad/skills/' is the consumer's library of custom interaction patterns and org-specific heuristics. update.js never touches this directory. The shipped skill library is 'skills/' (curated, framework-owned). '.copilot/skills/' contains process playbooks and is FRAMEWORK-owned (synced on update).
notes.package_json_policy: package.json is FRAMEWORK-owned — it drives the secops-squad CLI version and built-in dependencies. update.js WILL overwrite it on update. RISK: A consumer who added dependencies to package.json will lose them. Mitigation: (1) update.js should detect if the consumer's package.json has dependencies not in the upstream version and emit a WARNING listing them, prompting the user to re-add them manually. (2) The recommended pattern for consumer extensions is a separate package or plugin — not editing root package.json directly. This is a documented caveat in the README under 'Extending the CLI'. package-lock.json is ALSO framework-owned and will be replaced to ensure lockfile consistency.
notes.deletion_policy: update.js may only DELETE files that: (a) were previously synced as framework files (i.e. exist in the consumer's repo), AND (b) no longer exist in the upstream framework_paths set. update.js MUST NEVER delete files matching personal_paths, even if they appear in both the local repo and would be implied by a glob. Deletion of framework files is done by computing the diff between the upstream framework file list and the local file list — any local framework file absent upstream is a candidate for removal. Always prompt/warn before deletion unless --yes flag is passed.
notes.update_algorithm: update.js must: (1) Fetch starter-kit/main. (2) Enumerate all files at starter-kit/main using 'git ls-tree -r --name-only starter-kit/main'. (3) For each upstream file, check if it matches framework_paths (glob match). (4) If it matches, check personal_paths — if personal match, SKIP. (5) Otherwise: 'git checkout starter-kit/main -- <path>'. (6) For deletion: compute framework files present locally but absent upstream; for each, confirm it is NOT a personal_paths match, then delete. (7) Run 'npm install' to sync package-lock.json after package.json update. Glob matching should use the 'minimatch' package (already available via npm ecosystem) or a simple manual implementation using Node built-ins.
notes.glob_matching_note: The glob patterns in this manifest use standard minimatch/micromatch syntax. update.js may use the 'minimatch' package (add as dep if not present) or implement simple prefix/suffix matching for the common cases. The personal_paths check is the critical guard; when in doubt, err on the side of treating a file as personal.
notes.framework_exceptions_note: Paths in framework_exceptions are ALWAYS treated as framework-owned, even if they match a personal_paths glob. Used for fixed-identity agents (Scribe, Ralph) whose protocol charters are defined and maintained by the framework. classifyPath must check this array AFTER a personal_paths match and return 'framework' if the exact normalized path is present. Entries are exact paths (no globs); normalize backslashes to forward slashes before comparison.
